It agreed with the conclusion and then attacked the REASON GIVEN FOR IT, which is what the author had asked for: PR #25's whole case for classifying vendor output as shared is that it is only ever build output, verified by --check. It then found two ways --check could be satisfied by a tree that is not what the build produced. IT VERIFIED THE EXCEPTION DOES NOT LEAK, by comparing the classifier in main against the PR on every path, printed old -> new: hooks/hooks.json, bin/lwb_hook.py, .codex-plugin/plugin.json, skills/lwb-status/SKILL.md, bin/vendor_helper.py, plugins/codex/vendor/x.py and lwb/vendorx/x.py are all 'codex -> codex'. It also probed spellings the author had not: the bare 'vendor' directory without a trailing slash stays codex; backslash paths normalise correctly; './' prefixes, a leading '/' and 'plugins//codex' give 'other', WHICH CI REJECTS because check_lanes errors on any class that is neither shared nor the agent's own. HOLE 1, CONFIRMED, verbatim: 'a committed .pyc runs instead of the reviewed source, and --check cannot see it ... In a scratch package, an unchecked-hash .pyc under __pycache__/ printed payload even though the .py beside it said reviewed source. The same thing under plugins/*/lwb/vendor/ would ship via the plugin, and the diff a reviewer sees is a binary blob.' HOLE 2, CONFIRMED, verbatim: 'a file replaced by a same-named directory passes --check ... dircmp puts such mismatches in common_funny, which _trees_equal never checks. Making lwb_core/rules/lwb_version.py a directory holding payload.py gives trees_equal= True.' It added the honest qualifier itself: 'It can hide content but not run it: the core finds rules through normal imports, and nothing scans the directory.' ITS JUDGEMENT ON THE ALTERNATIVES, which the author had explicitly invited, verbatim: 'Shared-with-review is the safest of the three options. Vendoring only the calling agent's plugin leaves the other plugin stale, so --check fails, or passes stale code if the check is relaxed. Excluding vendor/ from the lane gate removes review entirely, leaving only --check and its holes (3, 4) as the guard.' It also noted the direction of travel: 'Before, each agent could commit into its own plugin's vendor/ with no review at all. Now every vendor change needs independent review.' PATH TRAVERSAL, PLAUSIBLE AND PRE-EXISTING, NOT INTRODUCED HERE, verbatim: 'plugins/codex/lwb/vendor/../bin/lwb_hook.py gives codex -> shared, and the write hook allows a claude Edit on it. But docs/../plugins/codex/lwb/bin/lwb_hook.py was already shared -> shared and allow on main. CI is not affected, because the lane gate reads canonical paths from git diff-tree --name-only.' ROUND 2, 5000101, after both holes were fixed: 'AGREE holds at 5000101. Both holes are closed.' It re-probed each -- the force-added .pyc gives rc=1 naming the file, the file-turned-directory gives rc=1 DRIFT from the new common_funny check, the unmodified tree rc=0 -- and confirmed an UNTRACKED .pyc correctly gives rc=0, since it cannot ship through git. IT THEN FOUND TWO MORE. FINDING 5, CONFIRMED, AND THE SHARPEST OF THE REVIEW, verbatim: 'Case variant, missed on Windows. A tracked .../rules/LWB_VERSION.PY (added to the index only) gives rc=0. Comparing against the set of staged relative paths instead of calling exists() would close it on every OS.' This is the inverse of the usual works-on-my-machine: the defect bit on the platform most contributors use and Linux CI would have caught it. The author reproduced it (returned [] where it should have named the file) and implemented the prescribed set comparison. FINDING 6, verbatim: 'Fails open on a git error ... if git fails, the stowaway check reports nothing and says nothing.' ROUND 3, c387368: 'AGREE holds at c387368. Finding 5 is fixed. IT NAMED THE PRECEDENT ITSELF: 'the same contradiction as the main SHA gate in #22'. That is what decided the fix.
